summary: Philip Whalen was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar. He earned a BA from Reed College (~1946–1951) and studied under Richard Baker in 1972. He served as head monk at Dharma Sangha (1984) and abbot at Hartford Street Zen Center (1991).

Philipp André Maas is an Indology and philosophy scholar who earned his Dr. phil. at the University of Bonn (1997–2004). His career includes positions at the University of Vienna (2010–2016), Leipzig (2016–2026), and a professorship at Munich (2024).

Philipp Keiper was an Iranian, Central Asian, and linguistics scholar. He earned his PhD at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1874–1877) under Friedrich von Spiegel and worked as a Gymnasium teacher, including at Herzog-Wolfgang-Gymnasium (1890).
Philipp Schäffer was a scholar in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied under Max Walleser and completed his Ph.D. at Heidelberg University between 1920 and 1924.

Philippe Colinet was an Indology, linguistics, and religious studies scholar. He completed his Ph.D. at KU Leuven (1881–1884) under Charles-Joseph de Harlez de Deulin, later serving there as eo. Professor (1887) and ordinary Professor (1889).

Philippe Stern was a history, archaeology, and Indology scholar who studied under Louis Finot (~1919–1925). He taught as Professor at École du Louvre (1929–1965) and served as Conservateur-en-chef at the Guimet Museum (1954–1965).

Philippe Turenne is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and completed his PhD at McGill University (attested 2010) under G. Victor Sōgen Hori.

Philippe Édouard Foucaux was an Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Eugène Burnouf. He held professorships at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales (from 1842) and the Collège de France (1857; 1870–1894).
Phillip Bloom is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Sinology. He completed his PhD at Harvard University under the supervision of Eugene Y. Wang, Yukio Lippit, and James Robson.
Philoxène Luzzatto was a scholar in Indology and linguistics who studied under Samuel David Luzzatto. He was a member of the Accademia Galileiana and the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft.
Phra Athiwat Thammawatsiri is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Ph.D. in Buddhist Studies from Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University, where he also served as a lecturer and researcher.

Phra Brahmapundit is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He served as Rector of Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (~1997–2018), President of the International Association of Buddhist Universities (~2007), and Chief Abbot at Wat Prayurawongsawat (~2008).

Phra Rajavaramuni is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University and Sukhothai Thammathirat Open University. He served as Dean of the Faculty of Buddhist Studies and Deputy Vice Rector at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (attested 2012).

Phra Sigambhirayan is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed a Bachelor of Liberal Arts at Sukhothai Thammathirat Open University and an M.A. in Buddhist Studies at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University.

Phramaha Niras Ruangsan is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned a Master of Buddhist Studies (2009) and a PhD (2015) at the University of Sydney, and held a post at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University in 2017.

Phramonchai Saitanaporn is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied under traditional teacher Phrathepyanmahamuni and completed a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Sydney under Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle (attested 2009).
Phrapongsak K. is a scholar of Buddhist studies. In 2015, he held posts as a visiting researcher at Ryukoku University and as an open-call researcher at the Buddhist Art and Culture Research Center.

Phuntsok Tashi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned a B.A. from Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, an MA from the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and held a post at the National Museum of Bhutan.

Phyllis Granoff is an Indology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies scholar who earned her Ph.D. at Harvard (~1969–1973) under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. She was a professor at McMaster University (~1976–2004) and Yale University (2004).
Pia Guerrini Bione was an Indology scholar. She studied at the Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa and its Classe di Lettere e Filosofia, earning her Dr.phil. between 1903 and 1907.
